description: AuthZEN Authorization API PoC — standards tracking baseline

standards.label: AuthZEN Authorization API 1.0
standards.impact: Core spec — defines the five-tuple (subject/resource/action/context/environment), the /access/v1/evaluation and /access/v1/evaluations endpoints, and the decision response format. All pkg/authzen types and handler implement this spec directly. Approved as OpenID Final Specification January 2026 (81-1 vote) — no further normative revision expected.
standards._triage: 2026-08-29: promoted from wg-draft to final-spec. Approved January 12, 2026. Previous tracking rev '2.0-ID2' was an Implementation Draft label used during review — the Final Specification is versioned 1.0. The five-tuple model and endpoints are stable; no breaking changes expected. implemented_rev updated to 1.0.

standards.label: AuthZEN Access Request and Approval Profile (AARP) 1.0
standards.impact: HIGH — extends AuthZEN 1.0 binary allow/deny with a third outcome: 'deny but requestable'. A PDP may respond that access is denied now but can be requested for approval. This outcome maps directly to pkg/authzen/pdp.go InMemoryPDP decision type — currently only ALLOW/DENY. Adding AARP adds a third decision variant: PENDING (access requestable). The approval-request flow would be implemented in a new pkg/authzen/aarp.go calling an approval endpoint. Demo would show the AARP scenario in the Token Exchange tab.
standards._triage: 2026-08-29: assessed. HIGH relevance. The 'deny but requestable' third outcome is absent from the current InMemoryPDP. No implementation yet — the two-value allow/deny model is insufficient for approval-gated scenarios. Add AARP as a tracked gap; implementation adds decision variant and approval request callout in demo.

standards.label: COAZ Framework 1.0 (Context-Oriented Authorization for Zero-Trust)
standards.impact: MEDIUM — formalises SARC (Subject, Action, Resource, Context) mapping as the canonical model for externalising authorization decisions to an AuthZEN PDP in a zero-trust context. The PoC's InMemoryPDP already implements the five-tuple model (subject/resource/action/context/environment) informally. COAZ Framework formalises the policy model, risk context propagation, and PDP trust boundary expectations. No implementation change required today — current model is compatible. Track for when WG stabilises the SARC vocabulary; may influence pkg/authzen/types.go field naming.
standards._triage: 2026-08-29: assessed. MEDIUM relevance. Current implementation is already COAZ-compatible informally. No urgent code change. Track for vocabulary alignment once WG stabilises.

standards.label: COAZ-MCP Binding 1.0
standards.impact: MEDIUM (here) / HIGH (wimse-agent-fabric) — binds AuthZEN PDP decisions to MCP tool calls. Primary implementation home is wimse-agent-fabric/internal/gateway/server.go. Tracked here for cross-project awareness: the PoC demonstrates the AuthZEN PDP side; the agent-fabric demonstrates the MCP enforcement side. No code change needed in authzen-poc — the PDP is already AuthZEN 1.0 compliant and can serve COAZ-MCP evaluation requests.
standards._triage: 2026-08-29: assessed. Tracked here for cross-project awareness. Primary home: wimse-agent-fabric. The authzen-poc InMemoryPDP is already a valid COAZ-MCP PDP — no code changes needed.

standards.label: AuthZEN Obligations Profile 1.0
standards.impact: MEDIUM — allows a PDP to attach mandatory machine-readable obligations to an ALLOW decision: 'log this action', 'require MFA', 'apply rate-limit'. The AuthZEN 1.0 decision response is a plain boolean (allow: true/false); Obligations Profile adds an 'obligations' array. pkg/authzen/pdp.go InMemoryPDP Decision struct would gain an Obligations []Obligation field. The demo Token Exchange tab would show obligations attached to decisions (e.g., 'require audit log entry' when the Txn-Token exchange is approved).
standards._triage: 2026-08-29: assessed. MEDIUM relevance. Current InMemoryPDP returns plain allow/deny — obligations are not expressed. Implementation adds Obligations []Obligation to the Decision response struct. Track for when WG stabilises obligation types.

standards.label: AuthZEN Profile for OAuth 2.0 Token Issuance
standards.impact: Defines how to map any OAuth token issuance decision to an AuthZEN PDP evaluation. The five-tuple model defined here is the canonical input to our InMemoryPDP. When adopted, implementation adds an AuthZEN client call at each token issuance decision point.

standards.label: AuthZEN Binding for OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange
standards.impact: Specifies how an RFC 8693 Token Exchange request (identity chaining, ID-JAG, Txn-Token) maps to an AuthZEN PDP evaluation. Directly implemented in the AS Bridge simulation (cmd/demo-wasm wasmSimulateAS): subject_token sub → subject.id, audience → resource.id, 'exchange' → action.name.

standards.label: OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange
standards.impact: Foundational. The AS Bridge simulation demonstrates exactly the RFC 8693 Token Exchange request structure (grant_type, subject_token, subject_token_type, audience). AuthZEN fills the 'local policy' gap RFC 8693 leaves undefined.

standards.label: OpenFGA DSL (Authorization Model)
standards.impact: pkg/authzen/export.go ToOpenFGA() generates an OpenFGA DSL model (schema 1.1) and YAML tuples from InMemoryPDP rules. The OpenFGA demo tab links to play.fga.dev with the generated model.

standards.label: Open Policy Agent — Rego policy language
standards.impact: pkg/authzen/export.go ToRego() generates a Rego v1 policy from InMemoryPDP rules. The OPA demo tab POSTs the policy to play.openpolicyagent.org share API to open it live.
